name: RELX PLC

profile.description: RELX is a global provider of information-based analytics and decision tools in four segments: Risk (LexisNexis Risk Solutions), Scientific, Technical & Medical (Elsevier), Legal (LexisNexis Legal & Professional) and Exhibitions (RX). In H1 2026 revenue was £4,871M with 7% underlying growth, led by Legal (+10%) and Risk (+8%), and the adjusted operating margin expanded to 35.5% [1]. The US ADR trades at $39.14, about $67.9B market cap [4].

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): RELX has turned generative AI into a growth driver. Lexis+ AI and the Protégé assistant pushed Legal to 10% underlying growth and 13% profit growth in H1 2026, and STM 'stepped up' to 6% [1][2]. AI Deployment (2/2): CEO Erik Engstrom says AI-enabled products now account for about 90% of the value of new LexisNexis sales, and Lexis+ with Protégé is 'continuing on the same penetration curve' [2]. Market Share (1/2): Elsevier's scholarly-publishing scale is large enough to have drawn a European Commission complaint alleging a dominant position, but LexisNexis competes head-to-head with Thomson Reuters and new AI entrants, and no hard share-gain data were found [3][2]. Pipeline (1/2): Management points to continued Protégé and agentic-AI roll-outs but gives no dated next-generation launches with revenue targets [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): Reported R&D was £364M in FY2024, 3.9% of revenue, below information-services and software peers [5].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): RELX frames its purpose as helping researchers, clinicians, lawyers and risk professionals make better decisions, and publishes a corporate-responsibility framework around customers and society. The statement is clear but reads as a description of its markets rather than a distinctive cause [6]. Community Impact (1/2): RELX runs group-wide corporate-responsibility and employee-giving programs [6], but no flagship foundation dollar figures were found, and a 2024 lawsuit by a former Cell Press employee alleges retaliation for raising climate 'greenwashing' concerns [3]. Employee Retention (0/2): No tenure or turnover data was found. Insider Buying (0/2): No director open-market buying was found. Capital return is instead via corporate buybacks, with £1.75B of a planned £2.25B deployed in 2026 [1].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Scored mechanically on Dividend-sleeve weights. ROE of 131.9% (1.0), forward P/E of 18.4 (1.0) and profit margin of 23.3% (1.0) all hit target [4]. Reported revenue growth of 2.7% scores 0.76; underlying growth was 7%, with sterling strength diluting reported figures [1][4]. The 2020-2025 revenue CAGR of 6.2% (£7.11B to £9.59B) scores 0.74 [5]. D/E of 709.6% scores 0 because years of buybacks have shrunk the equity base [4]. Payout ratio of 53.6% scores 0.77 [4]. The ADR has paid a dividend every year since 1995, scoring 1.0 at 2x weight. ADR dividends have risen for 10 straight calendar years (2016-2025), scoring 1.0. The 5-year ADR dividend CAGR of 6.9% ($0.59 to $0.82) scores 1.0 at 2x weight [4]. Weighted sum of 10.28 out of 12 gives an Infrastructure score of 9 (8.56). Liquidity floor cleared: 2.28M average volume x $39.14 = about $89M per day.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (5/9): RELX has been one of the stocks hit hardest by AI disruption fears. Shares fell about 17% amid AI-competition concerns and sit roughly 30% below their high even as profit rose 9%, and commentators flag frontier-model legal agents as direct competitors to Lexis+ AI [2][7]. Management's defense is proprietary, continuously updated legal, scientific and risk datasets that model makers cannot replicate, and so far growth has held, with Legal +10% and Risk +8% [1][2]. The core analytics business is defensible, but legal research and scientific publishing face real substitution and pricing risk. AI Opportunity (1/1): AI-enabled products drive about 90% of the value of new LexisNexis sales [2].

infinite_game.summary: RELX has steadily reinvented an old publishing franchise into a data-and-analytics compounder and is now leaning into generative AI. Sinek would note, though, that its purpose language is mostly market description and its competitive posture is defensive. Heavy buybacks (£2.25B planned for 2026) and margin-expansion targets point to a disciplined but partly finite, shareholder-return orientation.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): RELX ties its work to advancing science, health, the rule of law and fair risk decisions [6]. That connects to something bigger than profit, but it reads as a portfolio description, and the Elsevier competition complaint shows how the academic community sees its access model [3].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Leadership is stable and no major cultural red flags surfaced, but the 2024 Cell Press whistleblower-retaliation lawsuit and the lack of retention data keep this at average [3].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): RELX's public response to AI challengers is defensive. Executives emphasize that rivals cannot replicate its proprietary data rather than describing what competitors teach it [2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The company has steadily moved its products to AI-enabled tools, with AI products now driving about 90% of new LexisNexis sales value [2]. That is meaningful evolution, but in this cycle it is an upgrade of existing franchises rather than abandoning a core business.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Management kept investing in Lexis+ AI and Protégé while the shares de-rated on AI fears, and those products now drive Legal's acceleration [1][2]. At the same time, £2.25B of 2026 buybacks and a promise that profit will grow faster than revenue show a strong pull toward near-term shareholder returns [1].

investment_thesis: RELX is a high-margin, subscription-heavy analytics compounder whose AI investments are visibly paying off. H1 2026 underlying revenue grew 7%, underlying adjusted operating profit grew 9%, the margin rose to 35.5%, and adjusted EPS rose 11% at constant currency to 68.6p [1]. Legal accelerated to 10% growth on Lexis+ AI and Protégé, and AI-enabled products now drive about 90% of new LexisNexis sales value [2]. At 18.4x forward earnings, a 2.3% yield with 10 straight years of ADR dividend growth, and a 6.9% 5-year dividend CAGR [4], the AI-fear de-rating could be an entry point.
thesis_continued: The bear case is that generative AI erodes the pricing power of legal research and scientific publishing over time even if near-term growth holds. The shares remain about 30% below their high on that fear [7]. The balance sheet is levered for buybacks (D/E 710%, $8.9B debt vs. $220M cash) [4], reported revenue growth is only 2.7% after currency effects [4], and Elsevier faces ongoing criticism of its subscription model and data practices. The 2024 greenwashing and retaliation suit adds governance noise [3]. Exhibitions also carries Middle East event uncertainty [1].
key_catalysts: FY2026 results (February 2027) confirming underlying profit growth above revenue growth, as reaffirmed at H1 [1]
Continued Lexis+ AI / Protégé penetration sustaining Legal's 10% underlying growth and disproving AI-substitution fears [2]
Completion of the remaining £0.5B of the £2.25B 2026 buyback and a FY2026 dividend increase extending the growth streak [1][4]
key_risks: Frontier-model legal and research agents compressing LexisNexis and Elsevier pricing; the shares already trade about 30% below their high on this fear [7]
High leverage (D/E 710%) from buybacks limits flexibility if AI disruption hits cash flows [4]
Regulatory and reputational pressure on Elsevier's academic-publishing model and on LexisNexis Risk data-broker practices [3]
